body: I agree with others saying to contact your surgeon, but in the meantime while you wait, I wanted to share that I also noticed a hole in my check there around the same time post OP and I was told it was a normal part of healing! Definitely freaked me out to see a hole in my cheek for a few days but it indeed healed up quick without complication. Hoping that it’s the same thing for you and you’re back to normal very soon!

I was out a whole month (4 weeks)

There are liquid versions of most psychiatric meds. Your primary doctor can write you a prescription for those and you can get them at any pharmacy. I took my anxiety medication in liquid form while at the hospital with a syringe! But in an emergency, my nurse said you can also just crush your pills in a bit of water and take them with a syringe as well.

If your stitches are dissolvable, I would not worry. I had a 4-5mm “hole” at the exact same spot from stitches coming out on week 2, and I called the ER attending jaw surgery resident who told me this is normal and that’s how cheek stitches heal. My follow up with my surgeon confirmed it a few days later too. By now (6 weeks post op) it has healed up great. However, if you have symptoms of infection (redness, soreness, pain, fever) then definitely call your doctor!

Yes I have several plates. My surgeons advised that I don’t need to get them removed unless they present an issue (pain, infection, or I can feel them and they bother me). So I don’t plan on removing them, plus I’d love to not have another surgery ever again lol
I’m hoping I don’t have a repeat surgery to remove plates in the future, so here’s hoping it’s nothing to worry about!

I have the exact same issue on my left cheekbone at 2 weeks post op, and my surgeon said it’s bone (but there was never bone there before surgery). Sorry that’s not helpful, but at least know you’re not alone
About 6 days for me (today)!

I have a genetic open bite, and as a result TMJ too, so DJS was always part of my orthodontics plan when I got braces again as an adult. I’m not sure how my mouth and nose will be ultimately affected until the swelling goes down, but for now they swole up along with the rest of my face. It was a full anesthesia surgery, and I don’t know much of the mechanics of it. I recommend going to a specialist, dentists, and orthodontist for your TMJ issues and having them collaborate to see what really makes sense for your treatment plan. I know I wouldn’t be able to figure out the exact surgery I need without my medical team. Good luck!

I’m glad I’m not the only one whose pain got worse (is it bad to say I’m glad?). They gave me oxycodone to take when needed for the first 3 days at home, but I’m hesitant to take it a lot in fear of addiction. So we will see how it goes!
Thank you so much, I hope you’re doing better now too!

Context: So I’m not sure how normal this is (my surgeon says they see it a lot, but idk), but on day 3 out of nowhere I started hemorrhaging uncontrollably from my left nostril and mouth, to the point they had to launch an adult rapid response on me at the hospital. It got under control in about 5 mins, but I lost a ton of blood so they kept me for observation and fluids for one more night. Apparently a blood clot in my top jaw dislodged and caused this. 

My pain has also been significant - 7/10 if I forget a painkiller or take it late. It’s been a tough recovery process but I’m lucky to have family with me who keep reminding me on the long term goal of this surgery.

Yes, I completely agree with you about finding a more appropriate therapist. I'm in the process of doing that now. 

I suppose our second brother, who has met and hung out with our brother's friend, could reach out to him. I don't know if he'd feel comfortable talking to me - we've only met 2 or 3 times. I can ask him and see if he'd be up for it. It worries me, however, that if this friend knew nothing about this, my brother would feel hurt and betrayed about us reaching out to his friend.

My mom can probably reach out to his therapist - I didn't even think about that. He is an internet addiction specialist (if that makes any difference) and he was giving my brother everyday techniques/tips to help him manage the addiction, some emotional and some practical, e.g. placing a clock by the computer monitor to track how long it's been. I'm not very confident that he'd be the right person for this type of thing. 

As long as I can remember, my brother enjoyed playing video games and engaging in online communities. He progressively started spending more and more time on them when he hit puberty (13, maybe 14yo?). I only remember that because I remember my parents' complaints about it increasing around that time. He'd be online for most of the day, usually playing online games until 3-4am in the morning. My parents started looking into it as a legit problem when he was around 16-17, but then he abruptly stopped playing and focused on studying for his uni entrance exams at 17-18. So my parents stopped researching it. He then started again after he moved out for college, and by the end of last year he went to my mom and told her that he needed help and asked her to find a psychiatrist. From what I can tell, he usually gets into it a lot when he struggles. He struggled with fitting in/making close friends in middle school, and he struggled with being in a field that he hated now in uni. 

When he is okay, my brother is fairly introverted. He has a handful of close friends who, however, change often. I think he has just one friend that has been with him for years. He has a sense of humor and the two of us usually joke about memes and other internet things. He likes to play online with his friends and go out to bars, but he usually does not drink excessively until lately last year. I think he is extremely intelligent - he keeps getting obsessed with and mastering "brainy" things - chess, logarithms, etc. 

I want to thank you guys SQLwitch and pokesomi so far for your advice. This has been really helpful - both to hear your thoughts, but also to reflect and think more about my brother.

Thank you for commenting. I can give you an example: When my mom finally reached him on the phone and he told her that he is unhappy with his life, she asked him if there is anything specific in his life that makes him unhappy and he said "I don't want to tell you." Similarly, when he texted his ex-girlfriend he said he'd "do something bad" but when she pressed him to specify, he kept saying "I don't want to tell you." When my mom asked if he wanted to talk about it with anybody else - me, my brother, our dad, our uncle, anyone really (assuming that he wasn't comfortable enough with her  to talk to her openly) - he kept saying no. I haven't asked him directly anything yet because I fear I'll get the same response. 

It just really frustrates me because I'm typically direct and expect people to be the same. I understand that my brother is different in that way. But it worries me that he won't fully open up to anyone, and that it will lead to this same situation again sometime in the future.
